headline: Approved 2027 meeting calendar and September 2, 2026 minutes; discussed staffing, safety, and firefighter cancer concerns.
summary: Assistant Fire Chief Jeramine Atkinson was introduced after his appointment on October 13, 2026. Officials discussed department staffing, the Deputy Fire Marshal recruitment, and safety meetings. Members approved the 2027 meeting calendar and the minutes of the September 2nd, 2026 meeting.

decision_titles: Approval of minutes of the September 2nd, 2026 meeting
plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Fire Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
6:00 PM, October 21, 2026 
 
 
 
Memorial Town Hall 
2372 Whitney Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 The meeting was called to order by Chairman Commissioner G. Tinney at 6:04 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 The roll was taken by the Clerk, and the following members were: 
 
Present: 
Commissioner Gary Tinney, Chair 
Commissioner Robert Mordecai 
Commissioner Thomas A. Madera 
 
Absent 
Commissioner Nancy Jordan 
Commissioner Samod Rankins 
 
Also present were Chief Shelly Carter of the Hamden Fire Department and Briana J. 
Belton-Robinson, BC Clerk, along with Assistant Chief Jeramine Atkinson and Battalion 
Chief Paul Kobbe.  
 
Roll Call Summary: Present, Voting 3, Present, Not Voting 0, Absent 2, Excused 0. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 Commissioner R. Mordecai made a motion to approve the minutes of the September 2nd, 
2026 meeting. The motion was seconded by Commissioner T. Madera. 
 
The motion passed. 
 
Vote: All in favor, no nays, no abstentions. The previous meeting minutes were adopted 
unanimously. 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT
Chairman Commissioner G. Tinney opened the floor for public comment. 
 
No public comments were received. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE FROM THE OFFICE OF THE FIRE CHIEF 
  
 Fire Chief S. Carter provided the Commission with a departmental update addressing 
administrative leadership, staffing, recruitment, community risk reduction, training, and 
departmental operations. 
 
Appointment of Assistant Fire Chief 
 
Chief S. Carter formally introduced Assistant Fire Chief J. Atkinson, who was appointed on 
October 13, 2026. Assistant Chief J. Atkinson brings approximately 25 years of fire service 
experience and most recently served as Fire Chief of Stratford, Connecticut. 
 
Chief S. Carter stated that Assistant Chief J. Atkinson has begun visiting fire stations, 
accompanying Battalion Chiefs, and reviewing departmental administrative responsibilities. 
His appointment is expected to strengthen communication, officer development, 
operational oversight, and administrative efficiency. 
 
Chief S. Carter acknowledged the assistance of the Battalion Chiefs, who have assumed 
additional leadership responsibilities during the Department's period of reduced 
administrative staffing. 
 
Assistant Chief J. Atkinson thanked the Commission for the opportunity to serve and 
expressed his commitment to becoming familiar with departmental operations, engaging 
with personnel, and supporting continued improvements. 
 
Personnel and Staffing 
 
Chief S. Carter reported six departmental vacancies: four line positions and two 
administrative positions. These include two EMT positions, two paramedic positions, the 
Fire Marshal position, and the Deputy Fire Marshal position. 
 
The Department is working with Human Resources to fill the vacancies through established 
recruitment procedures. 
 
Chief S. Carter also discussed the possibility of lateral transfers for qualified firefighters. 
She noted that hiring experienced personnel could reduce the approximately $ 9,000-per-
recruit cost of firefighter training. 
 
Fire Marshal's Office 
 
Chief S. Carter reported that Fire Marshal Brian Dolan recently retired and that Brian Gilson 
is serving as Acting Fire Marshal. 
 
The Fire Marshal's Office continues its responsibilities despite staffing shortages. Chief S. 
Carter acknowledged the Acting Fire Marshal, fire inspector, and administrative personnel 
for maintaining office operations.
Recruitment for the Fire Marshal and Deputy Fire Marshal positions continues. 
 
Community Risk Reduction and Public Education 
 
Chief S. Carter discussed the Department's continued emphasis on community risk 
reduction and expanding public education beyond school-age children to include families, 
adults, and senior residents. 
 
The Department is developing seasonal fire safety outreach initiatives addressing 
Halloween safety, holiday cooking hazards, Christmas tree safety, and other preventable 
emergencies. 
 
The Department will distribute educational materials through fire apparatus, community 
organizations, churches, restaurants, and other locations throughout Hamden. 
 
Chief S. Carter also discussed strengthening partnerships with senior services and other 
municipal agencies to assist vulnerable residents, including individuals experiencing unsafe 
living conditions. 
 
Community Engagement 
 
Chief S. Carter reported attending a First Responders Mass and Green Harvest Sunday 
services, where she discussed fire prevention and community risk reduction. 
 
She expressed interest in expanding partnerships with faith-based organizations to provide 
fire safety education, CPR awareness, and additional community services. 
 
Chief S. Carter also recognized the personnel at Fire Station 2 for preparing Halloween 
decorations and engaging with the community. 
 
Training, Equipment, and Departmental Operations 
 
Chief S. Carter reported continued progress in officer development, departmental training, 
policy updates, and implementation of the Department's new records management system. 
 
The Department is also evaluating equipment replacement needs, including rescue 
apparatus, a tower ladder truck, staff vehicles, and significant fire station maintenance 
concerns. 
 
Chief S. Carter emphasized that aging apparatus and vehicles present operational and 
safety concerns and that replacing outdated equipment remains a departmental priority. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No Executive Session was held. 
7. REPORTS
A. Report of the Chairman  
  Firefighter Occupational Cancer Awareness and Legislative Advocacy 
 
Chairman G. Tinney discussed his recent travels throughout the country and 
expressed concern regarding the increasing number of firefighters diagnosed with 
various cancers associated with occupational exposures. 
 
Chairman G. Tinney stated that firefighters encounter hazardous substances and 
environmental exposures throughout their careers, some of which may contribute to 
long-term health complications. 
 
He reported working with other individuals and organizations to research firefighter 
occupational cancers, identify support resources, and advocate for federal legislation 
addressing firefighter health and safety. 
 
Chairman G. Tinney referenced federal legislative efforts involving Senator Cory 
Booker and Congressman Darren Soto intended to strengthen protections and 
resources for firefighters affected by occupational cancers. 
 
He emphasized the importance of supporting firefighters throughout their careers and 
ensuring that personnel receive appropriate recognition, respect, and protection. 
 
Sound Off Fire Safety Education Program 
 
Chairman G. Tinney provided an update on the Sound Off program, a national 
interactive fire safety education initiative designed for school-age children. 
 
He explained that the program includes an educational curriculum delivered through 
classroom teachers, incorporating interactive exercises and activities to teach children 
about fire prevention, smoke alarms, and home safety. 
 
The program also encourages students to share fire safety information with parents, 
grandparents, and other household members. 
 
Chairman G. Tinney reported that approximately 170 smoke detectors equipped with 
10-year batteries will be distributed through the program's outreach efforts. 
 
He further reported that the Superintendent of Hamden Public Schools had contacted 
him regarding the initiative and expressed interest in its implementation. 
 
Chairman G. Tinney stated that he would provide Commissioners with additional 
program materials, including curriculum information and educational posters. 
  B. Personnel Roster  
  Chief S. Carter reviewed departmental staffing levels and recruitment efforts. 
 
The Department currently has four line vacancies and two vacancies in the Fire 
Marshal's Office. 
 
Chief S. Carter reported that the Department employs 18 paramedics, with one
currently without medical control authorization. 
 
She explained that the next two positions to be filled are expected to require 
paramedic qualifications. 
 
The Department continues working with Human Resources to evaluate recruitment 
opportunities, including lateral transfers, while maintaining compliance with municipal 
hiring requirements. 
 
 
 
  C. Fire Marshall Office Report  
  Deputy Fire Marshal Recruitment and Promotional Opportunities 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai raised concerns regarding the recruitment process for the 
Deputy Fire Marshal position. 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai stated that he attended a Civil Service Commission 
meeting and learned that the Town was considering external applicants for the 
position. 
 
He questioned why the Department was recruiting outside the organization when 
internal personnel may be interested in advancement opportunities. 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai expressed concern that requiring applicants to have 
attained the rank of Lieutenant or Captain could limit opportunities for otherwise 
qualified firefighters seeking career advancement. 
 
He said he had contacted the union about the availability of internal candidates and 
asked how the Department could effectively retain personnel if promotional 
opportunities were not available from within. 
 
Chief S. Carter responded that the recruitment process must comply with the Town of 
Hamden's Civil Service rules, applicable collective bargaining agreements, and 
established hiring procedures. 
 
She explained that Civil Service determines the appropriate recruitment process and 
that the Fire Chief does not independently control those decisions. 
 
Chief S. Carter reported that the Deputy Fire Marshal recruitment process included 11 
applicants: two internal and nine external. 
 
She stated that the Deputy Fire Marshal job description was established in 2014 
under the administration of then-Acting Fire Chief David Berardesca. The position's 
existing qualifications include rank and professional experience requirements. 
 
Chief S. Carter explained that she did not believe it appropriate to independently lower 
established qualifications solely to expand the applicant pool.
She further stated that Human Resources was reviewing whether applicable time-in-
grade provisions or other established procedures could give internal applicants 
additional consideration. 
 
Chief S. Carter offered to meet with Commissioner R. Mordecai and union 
representatives that evening or the following morning to discuss their concerns and 
clarify the recruitment process. 
 
She said she would share additional information from Human Resources with the 
Commission. 
  D. Good and Welfare of the Department   
  Departmental Leadership and Administrative Responsibilities 
 
Chief S. Carter discussed the challenges of overseeing departmental operations while 
serving without an Assistant Fire Chief for approximately two years. 
 
She said that managing personnel, developing policies, coordinating training, 
addressing safety concerns, overseeing equipment needs, and maintaining 
community engagement placed significant demands on the Office of the Fire Chief. 
 
Chief S. Carter emphasized that the appointment of Assistant Chief J. Atkinson will 
allow for a more effective distribution of administrative and operational responsibilities. 
 
She said her goal is to improve departmental communication, strengthen personnel 
support, maintain operational readiness, and ensure firefighters have the resources 
needed to perform their duties safely. 
 
Department Mechanics and Maintenance Staffing 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai raised concerns about recruiting mechanics from outside 
the Department's existing personnel structure. 
 
Chief S. Carter acknowledged the Shop Department's efforts to recruit mechanics 
externally. 
 
She reiterated the importance of maintaining operational efficiency, supporting 
departmental personnel, and ensuring that staffing decisions comply with established 
municipal procedures. 
 
Training Division and Training Officer Coverage 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai asked about the status of Training Officer Lopes, who was 
on leave, and who would coordinate departmental training during his absence. 
 
The Commission discussed the importance of maintaining training continuity and 
ensuring that firefighters continue receiving required instruction, certifications, and 
professional development opportunities. 
 
Chief S. Carter stated that departmental training, officer development, and policy
updates remain priorities and will receive additional administrative support from 
Assistant Chief J. Atkinson. 
 
Departmental Safety Meetings and Workplace Injuries 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai expressed concern about suspending the Department's 
regular safety meetings. 
 
He questioned whether the absence of these meetings could contribute to workplace 
injuries and referenced a recent firefighter injury at Fire Station 5. 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai emphasized the importance of annual safety meetings, 
employee participation, hazard identification, and consistent follow-up on workplace 
safety concerns. 
 
Chief S. Carter acknowledged that the department temporarily suspended formal 
safety meetings because of administrative staffing limitations. 
 
However, she explained that safety oversight has continued through regular 
communication with Battalion Chiefs, review of employee injury reports, and 
coordination with the Town's Risk Management, Workers' Compensation, Public 
Works, and Building Maintenance personnel. 
 
Chief S. Carter stated that she communicates frequently with Battalion Chiefs 
regarding injuries, workplace hazards, operational risks, and conditions requiring 
corrective action. 
 
Regarding the injury at Fire Station 5, Chief S. Carter reported that she had 
addressed the matter with the appropriate municipal departments. The department 
ordered replacement doors and temporarily secured the affected area pending 
repairs. 
 
She also reported that Assistant Chief J. Atkinson will coordinate departmental safety 
meetings and related administrative oversight. 
 
Chief S. Carter anticipated that regular safety meetings would resume within 
approximately one to two weeks. 
 
Paramedic Staffing and Medical Control 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai requested clarification regarding the number of 
paramedics currently employed by the Department and whether all paramedics had 
obtained medical control authorization. 
 
He questioned whether any personnel were performing paramedic duties without the 
required authorization. 
 
Chief S. Carter confirmed that the Department has 18 paramedics and that one 
individual had not yet obtained medical control authorization.
Chief S. Carter agreed to provide the Commission with regular updates identifying 
how many paramedics have obtained medical control and whose authorization 
remains pending. 
 
She reiterated that the next two planned hires are expected to be paramedics. 
 
Professionalism and Departmental Priorities 
 
Chief S. Carter emphasized the importance of professionalism, mutual respect, and 
keeping the Department focused on public service. 
 
Despite internal challenges and staffing concerns, she said the Department's primary 
responsibility remains protecting Hamden residents. 
 
Chief S. Carter expressed confidence that adding Assistant Chief J. Atkinson and 
continuing collaboration with departmental personnel would strengthen operations and 
improve service delivery. 
 
Correspondence Recognizing Fire Department Personnel 
 
Chief S. Carter presented correspondence dated October 7, 2026, from a retired fire 
department chaplain expressing appreciation for the Hamden Fire Department's 
response to a serious motor vehicle accident on Route 10 on or about October 4, 
2026. 
 
The correspondence acknowledged the Department's compassionate and 
professional response to the accident, which resulted in one fatality and one individual 
sustaining injuries requiring continued recovery. The writer, a former fire chaplain in 
Meriden, Connecticut, and Charlotte, North Carolina, commended the responding 
personnel for their emergency care and credited their efforts as instrumental in the 
surviving individual's outcome. 
 
Chief S. Carter shared the letter with the Commission to recognize the responding 
firefighters' dedication, professionalism, and commitment to public service. 
  E. Citizen Complaints  
  No additional citizen complaints were reported during the meeting. 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 Fire Commission Identification Badges and Apparel 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai revisited the discussion regarding identification badges for Fire 
Commissioners. 
 
He referenced the September 2, 2026, Special Meeting, where the Commission discussed 
procedures for issuing and returning metal identification badges. 
 
The proposed procedure would require Commissioners to acknowledge receipt of their 
badges and return them at the end of their terms so the Commission could reissue them to
future Commissioners. 
 
Commissioner R. Mordecai emphasized the practical importance of Commissioners having 
appropriate identification when representing the Commission or assisting members of the 
public. 
 
He described a recent incident in which he stopped to assist an elderly motorist whose 
vehicle had become disabled. He explained that an identification badge could have 
established his official affiliation and reassured the individual. 
 
Chief S. Carter said she understood the importance of identification badges but had not yet 
received specific direction on the proposed issuance and return procedures. 
 
She indicated that the Commission could develop a formal policy if directed. 
 
Chief S. Carter also reported that the Commission ordered identification apparel and 
expected it to arrive. 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  A. Approval of the 2027 Fire Commission Meeting Calendar  
  Chairman G. Tinney presented the proposed calendar for the 2027 Fire Commission 
meetings. 
 
Regular meetings will continue to be held on the third Wednesday of each month. 
 
The proposed meeting dates were as follows: 
 
Month Meeting Date 
January Wednesday, January 20, 2027 
February Wednesday, February 17, 2027 
March Wednesday, March 17, 2027 
April Wednesday, April 21, 2027 
May Wednesday, May 19, 2027 
June Wednesday, June 16, 2027 
July Wednesday, July 21, 2027 
August Wednesday, August 18, 2027 
September Wednesday, September 15, 2027 
October Wednesday, October 20, 2027 
November Wednesday, November 17, 2027 
December Wednesday, December 15, 2027 
 
Commissioner T.A. Madera made a motion to approve the 2027 Fire Commission 
meeting calendar as presented. Commissioner R. Mordecai seconded the motion. 
There was no further discussion.
Vote by Roll Call: 
Yes 
Commissioner Gary Tinney, Chair 
Commissioner Thomas A. Madera 
Commissioner Robert Mordecai 
 
No 
 
Absent 
Commissioner Samod Rankins  
Commissioner Nancy Jordan 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
 
Vote Summary: Yes 3, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 2 
10. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 The motion to adjourn passed unanimously. 
 
With no further business, the meeting adjourned at 6:55 PM.
